Country.evidence_source:
Full provided text: "2.2.5. Positive orientation
The Positivity Scale (P Scale; Caprara et al., 2012; Polish translation: Łaguna et al., 2011) was used. The participants' task was to rate the extent to which they agree with each statement on a 5 point scale, ranging from 1 (Strongly disagree) to 5 (Strongly agree). Scores on all 8 items were computed by averaging; higher results represent higher levels of positive orientation. Scores on the Polish P Scale showed a one-factor solution with good fitindices, adequate convergent validity, and internal consistency (Łaguna et al., 2011). Here, Cronbach ˛ was .87."

section_summary.extract_value: This section (2.2.5) describes the use of the Positivity Scale (P Scale) translated into Polish to measure positive orientation. It reports scoring (average of 8 items on a 1–5 scale) and internal consistency (Cronbach ˛ = .87). The section does not reference any study numbering, sample characteristics, BMI, body appreciation measures, or survey administration method.
